input.quote: This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein or unless either Client or TrueLink deliver to the other written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
input.rationale: Section 13 (p0078) provides automatic renewal for successive one-year terms with a mutual 30-day non-renewal notice window, which already meets the preferred renewal term length (12 months) and opt-out window (30 days). However, two elements of the preferred position are absent: there is no vendor reminder ahead of renewal, and there is no cap on renewal-term price increases — the only pricing protection is the one-year fee freeze in Section 6 (p0047), which expires before the first renewal, leaving uplift uncapped thereafter. Redline adds a 60-day TrueLink renewal reminder and caps renewal fee increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, with a 5% flat cap offered as fallback.

proposal.summary: Add vendor renewal reminder (60 days) and cap renewal price increases at lesser of CPI and 3%
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 30-day non-renewal window and one-year renewal term work for us, but we have added a 60-day renewal reminder from TrueLink and a cap on renewal-term fee increases at the lesser of CPI and 3%, consistent with our position that renewals be predictably priced and easy to exit. If helpful, we can accept a flat 5% cap as a fallback.

ops.oldText: no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year.
ops.newText: no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year. TrueLink will notify Client in writing of each upcoming renewal no later than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current term. Fees for any renewal term will not increase by more than the lesser of (i) the percentage increase in the U.S. Consumer Price Index over the preceding twelve (12) months and (ii) three percent (3%), in each case measured against the fees in effect during the immediately preceding term.
